description: HTML presentation rules from references/slides-*.md. Web-UI, pointer, and polish gates apply to a deck too - these are the ones specific to slides.

gates.title: One Idea Per Slide
gates.rule: Each slide carries a single point. A slide with three arguments is three slides.

gates.title: Headline States The Takeaway
gates.rule: The headline says the conclusion, not the topic. 'Revenue doubled in Q3', not 'Q3 Revenue'.

gates.title: Layout Comes From The Pattern Library
gates.rule: The slide uses a layout from references/slides-layout-patterns.md, chosen for its content shape rather than defaulting to title-and-bullets throughout.

gates.title: Deck Rhythm Varies
gates.rule: Consecutive slides do not share a layout. A deck of identical slides reads as a template.

gates.title: Chart Type Matches The Claim
gates.rule: The chart supports the headline's claim, and its type matches the data shape. Chart.js defaults are overridden to the deck's tokens.

gates.title: Every Figure Is Real
gates.rule: No number on a slide the user did not supply. A placeholder is marked as one.

gates.title: Readable At Presentation Size
gates.rule: Body type reads from the back of a room - nothing under 18px at 1920x1080, and no text sitting outside the safe margin.

gates.title: Deck Uses Design Tokens
gates.rule: Colour, type, and spacing come from the deck's token block, so every slide agrees. The validator runs clean: python3 scripts/system/slide-token-validator.py.

gates.title: Copy Follows The Formulas
gates.rule: Headlines, transitions, and closers are built with the formulas in references/slides-copywriting-formulas.md, then held to avoid-ai-writing.

gates.title: Speaker Notes Carry What The Slide Does Not
gates.rule: The detail that would clutter the slide lives in the notes, and the notes go through the copy pass too.

gates.title: Deck Renders At 16:9 And Prints
gates.rule: Checked at presentation size and in print or PDF export, since a deck usually travels as both.
